question: Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India are said to be "borrowed" from the citizen's duties enumerated in the constitution of _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**USSR**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India were borrowed from the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR).
 
• The 42nd Amendment to the Constitution in 1976 added these duties, which were originally ten in number.
 
• The 86th Amendment in 2002 added an eleventh duty, requiring parents and guardians to ensure their children receive an education between the ages of six and fourteen. 

 The Fundamental Duties are a reminder to citizens that they have duties to their nation, society, and other citizens in addition to their rights.
 
• They are non-justiciable and non-enforceable, and are difficult to define and measure.
 
• For example, the duty to "defend the country and render national service" is vague and could be interpreted in many ways
